content:
Here are the five FIFA World Cup Finals with the highest recorded attendances, **filtered so that each winning nation appears only once**:

| Rank | Final (Year, Venue) | Attendance | Winner | Confederation |
|------|---------------------|------------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | 1970 – Estadio Azteca, Mexico City | 114,000 | **Brazil** | CONMEBOL |
| 2 | 1954 – Wankdorf Stadium, Bern | 110,000 | **Switzerland** | UEFA |
| 3 | 1974 – Wankdorf Stadium, Bern (again) | 96,000 | **West Germany** | UEFA |
| 4 | 1978 – Estadio Monumental, Buenos Aires | 94,000 | **Argentina** | CONMEBOL |
| 5 | 1966 – Wembley Stadium, London | 96,000 | **England** | UEFA |

**Why this list is “without repeats”**

- The original top‑five attendance list would have had Brazil twice (1970 and 1994).  
- To keep each winner unique, the 1994 final (Brazil) was replaced by the next‑highest‑attendance final that had a different champion – the 1966 final (England).

Thus, the five distinct champions with the largest final‑match crowds are Brazil, Switzerland, West Germany, Argentina, and England, all hailing from either **CONMEBOL** (Brazil, Argentina) or **UEFA** (Switzerland, West Germany, England).
